newsitem.title: ST VINCENT: CRICKET-LARA ENDS LEAN SPELL WITH 10TH TEST CENTURY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LARA ENDS LEAN SPELL WITH 10TH TEST CENTURY.

text.p: Brian Lara returned to form with his 10th test century for West Indies on Monday to set up the prospect of a compelling climax to the short series against Sri Lanka.
Lara stroked 115 in West Indies' second innings total of 343 on the fourth day of the second and last test, leaving Sri Lanka 269 to win.
The touring team were 97 for two at the close, needing 172 more on Tuesday's final day to square the series. West Indies won the first test in Antigua by six wickets.
Aravinda de Silva was leading Sri Lanka's victory bid with a belligerent, unbeaten 34, containing seven fours, off just 28 balls.
Opener Sanath Jayasuriya (17) and Marvan Atapattu (10) were the two batsmen to fall, both bowled by West Indies' captain Courtney Walsh.
Lara, having made 0, 4 and 1 in his three previous innings in the series, played the dominant role when West Indies resumed at their overnight 128 for two, 53 ahead.

The Trinidadian left-hander reached three figures in 170 deliveries, and altogether faced 207 balls and batted 266 minutes, hitting 11 fours and one six as he took his test aggregate to 4,004 in 45 matches.
Lara, who started the day on 30 with just a lone boundary, reeled off nine scintillating fours and a six in the 58 runs he made in the morning.
After reaching his half-century off 102 balls, Lara accelerated, hitting off-spinner Muttiah muralitharam for three off-side fours in the final over before lunch.
However, Muralitharan and his off-spinning partner Kumara Dharmasena triggered a middle order collapse in which four wickets fall for 46 runs.
Dharmasena got the prized wicket of Lara, who whipped a delivery from middle stump straight into the hands of Jayasuriya at short mid-wicket.
Roland Holder (34) and Curtly Ambrose (31) added 53 for the eighth wicket on either side of tea before Muralitharan returned to wrap up the innings, finishing with five for 113.
